As the search engine used by thousands of federal websites, SearchGov supports more than 200 million searches a year. SearchGov shares its history with USA.gov , beginning when internet entrepreneur Eric Brewer donated a powerful search engine to the government. The interplay of temperature and daylight activates these changes and the subsequent plant and animal responses. A slight shift in any of these may mean that vegetation will no longer grow in a certain location or appear at a different time of year. Without plants, animals who eat them may struggle to survive or may have to move elsewhere to find better food. The consequences may extend to the entire ecosystem, including humans. In both Skagway and Nome, everyone agreed that spring is arriving earlier and fall is starting later. This not only makes for a longer growing season for gardeners, but it affects the arrival and departure timing of migratory animals that people hunt and may shift the location of where the animals are found. pages.title: See how ancient Indigenous artists left their mark on the landscape | National Geographic
pages.description: For millennia, Indigenous peoples etched and painted their stories across present-day North America. Today, everyone can still learn from that rich cultural heritage.
pages.text: See how ancient Indigenous artists left their mark on the landscape | National Geographic By Kate Nelson Photographs and video by Stephen Alvarez Published April 16, 2024 There is so much we don’t know for certain about ancient Indigenous artwork. When precisely was it made? What exactly did it mean to its creators? And yet there is still so much to be learned from these works carved into rock, painted on stone, drawn in mud, or built into the Earth’s surface. Perhaps most important is that thriving Native American societies, including my own, have inhabited Turtle Island, as many tribal peoples prefer to call North America, for tens of thousands of years. ( North America’s Native nations reassert their sovereignty: ‘We are here’. ) Considered alongside a contemporary Native reckoning—with historic Indigenous representation across everything from politics to pop culture—these sophisticated petroglyphs , pictographs, and geoglyphs help connect our past to present to future. For Native-descendant communities, this art represents a return home and a revitalization of the traditional lifeways that were all but destroyed by colonialism. On a narrow peninsula above the confluence of Rochester Wash and Muddy Creek, this sacred site is home to 13 panels of Barrier Canyon- and Fremont-style petroglyphs and pictographs. What scientific and technical information supports reviews? What Are Particulate Matter (PM) Air Quality Standards? National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for PM pollution specify a maximum amount of PM to be present in outdoor air. There are different standards for PM 10 and PM 2.5 (see Particulate Matter (PM) Basics to learn about particle types). Limiting PM pollution in the air protects human health and the environment. See NAAQS for PM for an in-depth explanation of the current PM standards, including Federal Register citations and fact sheets. How Are PM Standards Developed and Reviewed? The Clean Air Act requires EPA to set national air quality standards for particulate matter, as one of the six criteria pollutants considered harmful to public health and the environment. The law also requires EPA to periodically review the standards to ensure that they provide adequate health and environmental protection, and to update those standards as necessary. pages.text: Shoplifting measures welcomed by Birmingham traders Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Shoplifting measures welcomed by traders 4 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Bob Hockenhull West Midlands Getty Images The government pilot in the West Midlands will focus on prolific offenders Shopkeepers in the West Midlands have welcomed the announcement of new measures to cut shoplifting. The region is one of 16 police force areas chosen as part of a government pilot to target prolific retail offenders, which could see persistent thieves tagged and banned from high streets. Mani Gill, vice-chair of the Soho Road Business Improvement District (BID), Birmingham, said shoplifting was a daily occurrence, with small businesses least able to absorb the costs. Alex Goss, lead for retail crime at the National Police Chief's Council , said he welcomed the pilot to tackle prolific retail crime offenders "who continue to cause harm to businesses, retail workers and local communities". The new measures announced by the Home Secretary on Wednesday will focus on about 500 of the country's most prolific offenders, who the government said were "responsible for a disproportionate amount of shop theft". It said they could face restrictions on their movements including the use of GPS tags, along with being banned from the high street. NPS Photo / L. Zaragoza Serpentine Hot Springs is the most visited site in Bering Land Bridge National Preserve, but it can still be a challenging place to visit. Backcountry permits are not issued; people are able to visit on their own accord. There are no roads that lead into or within the preserve, and visitors may arrive by foot, boat, bike, small airplane, or snowmobile. Geographic Coordinates: 65.8569N, 164.7142W Modes of Transportation Aircraft Visitors usually reach Serpentine Hot Springs by air taxi or small private planes. Small aircrafts can land on an unmaintained gravel airstrip, which is a short walk from the bunkhouse, outhouse, and hot springs bathhouse. DinoData is a web-based tag editor for OpenStreetMap nodes, ways and relations, designed for phones first. Open an object, see what it is and what each tag means in your language, edit the tags with inputs suited to them, and save as a changeset . Geometry is not edited. It runs entirely in the browser and is hosted on Wikimedia Toolforge. It started as a Wikidata editor; the OpenStreetMap mode lives next to it in the same app. Finding an object Search for a place, or paste what you have: an openstreetmap.org URL (including edit and API URLs), an iD or JOSM remote control link, a short ID like n123 or way 123 , or coordinates. Other text is a place search with Photon and Nominatim . “Near me” lists the tagged objects around you via the Overpass API , handy while surveying. Close simon04's Diary OSM formats compared with TOML Posted by simon04 on 4 November 2026 in English . OSM formats compared with TOML OpenStreetMap data comes in several text formats. OSM XML is exact but verbose, OSM JSON has no comments, and Level0L is easy to type but has no grammar beyond its parser. TOML has comments, a spec and parsers in most languages, including Python’s standard library. So what would OSM data look like as TOML? I came across this question while adding an OSM tag editor to DinoData . Below, each format is compared with TOML using the examples from the OSM wiki, and the TOML versions are checked with Python’s tomllib . Level0L is the text format of the Level0 editor. DinoData reads and writes it in the OSM text view ( src/osm/level0.ts , src/osm/tags.ts ). It looks a bit like TOML : key = value lines, # comments, and headers that start a section. But the two formats are not compatible. This page compares them, together with the other formats DinoData meets, and shows how OSM data could look as TOML. Level0L (lines of text): editing in Level0. It calculates scopes 1, 2, and 3 emissions based on an organization’s activity data for one annual period. Intended Audience The calculator is intended for organizations interested in developing a GHG inventory. While it can be used by organizations of all sizes, it is primarily intended for small- to medium-sized organizations who are in the early stages of GHG management. The document is tailored to the smallest of businesses — those with no employees other than the owner, or "non-employer" firms as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration. These firms are also often colloquially referred to as "solopreneurs." While written for non-employer firms, the information in this document will also be useful to businesses with very few employees or with minimal IT infrastructure. The goal is to introduce the fundamentals of a small business cybersecurity program in non-technical language to set a solid cybersecurity risk management foundation. Considerations for maturing cybersecurity risk management as the business scales are included, which also makes the document useful for entities of varying sizes. Sobre los defectos de nacimiento Para todos 10 de nov. del 2026 English (US) Puntos clave Los defectos de nacimiento son cambios estructurales que están presentes al nacer. Los defectos de nacimiento pueden variar de condiciones médicas leves a graves. Los defectos de nacimiento pueden diagnosticarse durante el embarazo o después del nacimiento. Lo que son Los defectos de nacimiento son cambios estructurales que están presentes al nacer y que pueden afectar casi cualquier parte del cuerpo, como el corazón, el cerebro o los pies. Pueden afectar la apariencia y el funcionamiento del cuerpo, o las dos cosas. El lenguaje es importante. Si bien "defecto de nacimiento" es un término médico, no significa que una persona sea "defectuosa". Se refiere a condiciones que se presentan en un bebé antes del nacimiento.
